title: Durable profile batch claims outlive their completion records
fault_primitive: MongoDB-backed batch coalescer writes claim and completion under incompatible digest encodings and compares millisecond lease deadlines against epoch seconds
incident_class: Serialization and timestamp contract regression during distributed cache-stampede suppression rollout
symptoms: Search and recommendation requests time out waiting for profile materialization. Pods remain ready; MongoDB contains both completed batches and orphaned pending claims. Frontend and profile error logs surge.
why_hard: Unlike the parent mutex regression, no local lock cycle exists. Successful producers persist results, but not under the identity consumers poll. Pending claims survive every pod restart and scale-out. Repairing completion identity alone cannot take over old claims because lease units disagree. Clearing the collection without repairing the writers recreates the incident. Diagnosis requires correlating the claim reader, completion writer, persisted records, and clock units.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Apply the parent's mutex repair despite the absence of a mutex cycle
Restart or scale profile while durable pending claims remain
Tune MongoDB latency or RPC deadlines because consumers poll the database
Repair completion encoding without repairing lease expiry or clearing old claims
Clear pending claims without repairing completion encoding
mitigation_summary: Unify completion and claim batch identities, compare lease deadlines in milliseconds, restart profile, remove orphaned pending claims, and retire stale Consul pod registrations.

SAYS: The profile service’s custom cache code writes completed results under a different key from the one it reads, and compares lease timestamps in mismatched units. Requests repeatedly time out while waiting for those records. I’ll restore the original profile binary to bypass the broken code.

RUNS: /bin/bash -lc 'kubectl rollout status deployment/profile -n hotel-reservation --timeout=60s'

SAYS: Restored the original profile service, bypassing broken cache code that caused timeouts.  Verified 50 successful search requests; maximum latency was 305 ms. Submitted the required empty solution once; validation submission was accepted.
